explanation: Partition the current range into values greater than, equal to and less than a pivot. Keep only the partition containing the zero-based rank k−1 in descending order. Three-way partitioning handles repeated values efficiently and rearranges the input.
timeComplexity: O(n) average time; O(n^2) worst-case time for unfavorable pivots.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Three-way partitioning puts every value greater than the pivot before an equal block and every smaller value after it. The target’s descending rank therefore determines whether to keep the left partition, the right partition or return from the equal block. Discarded partitions cannot contain the requested rank.
walkthrough: For k=3 and [4,10,7,10,2], a pivot of 7 separates [10,10], [7] and [4,2]. The zero-based target rank 2 lies in the equal block, so return 7.
edgeCases: Count equal values separately in the ranking.
The method rearranges the supplied array.
k=1 and k=n request the maximum and minimum respectively.
